section: Laws for women - Dowry Prohibition Act, Domestic Violence Act 2005, POSH Act 2013, Maternity Benefit Amendment

accepted.s: Under Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the term ‘dowry’ refers to:
o: Only property demanded by the bride’s family before marriage
Property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage
Any gift exchanged between the spouses after marriage, including mahr
Only cash or movable property given after marriage
accepted.x: Dowry includes property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage, in connection with the marriage. Dower or mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded.
accepted.tq: Test the exact statutory definition and distinguish the excluded term.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Section 3 — Giving, taking or abetting dowry
Section 8A — Burden of proof on the accused
Section 8B — Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the Central Government
accepted.x: Section 8B provides for Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Government, not the Central Government. Sections 3, 4 and 8A are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong authority attached to a statutory power.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: The minimum punishment prescribed for giving, taking or abetting the giving or taking of dowry under Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act is:
o: Imprisonment of six months and fine up to ₹10,000
Imprisonment of not less than five years and fine of not less than ₹15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more
Imprisonment up to five years and fine up to ₹15,000
Imprisonment of two years and fine equal to the value of the dowry
accepted.x: Section 3 prescribes imprisonment of not less than five years and a fine of not less than ₹15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more. Five years is the minimum, not the maximum.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a statutory minimum from an apparent maximum.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: With reference to demanding dowry under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, which of the following is correct?
o: Imprisonment from six months to two years and fine up to ₹10,000
Imprisonment from two to five years without any fine
Imprisonment of not less than five years and fine of ₹15,000
Imprisonment up to six months and fine equal to the dowry value
accepted.x: Section 4 deals with demanding dowry and prescribes imprisonment from six months to two years, along with a fine up to ₹10,000.
accepted.tq: Separate the punishment for demanding dowry from the more severe punishment under Section 3.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding offences under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961:
1. The offences are cognisable.
2. The offences are non-bailable.
3. The offences are non-compoundable.
4. The burden of proof lies on the accused.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The offences are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. Section 8A places the burden of proof on the accused; therefore all four statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check each legal characteristic separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: A court taking cognisance of an offence under the Dowry Prohibition Act may act on its own knowledge or on a complaint made by:
o: Only the Dowry Prohibition Officer appointed by the State Government
Only the aggrieved woman’s immediate relatives
Only the police officer investigating the case
A recognised welfare body, among other permissible sources
accepted.x: Courts may act on their own knowledge or on complaints made by recognised welfare bodies. The provision is not restricted exclusively to police, relatives or Dowry Prohibition Officers.
accepted.tq: Identify the legally recognised source of a complaint without adding an exclusivity condition.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to dowry-related criminal law after the transition from the IPC to the BNS?
o: Dowry death — BNS Section 80; corresponding IPC Section 304B
Cruelty — BNS Section 80; corresponding IPC Section 498A
Presumption of dowry death — BNS Section 85; corresponding Evidence Act Section 113B
Dowry death — BNS Section 86; corresponding IPC Section 304B
accepted.x: Dowry death is covered by BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B. Cruelty is covered by BNS Sections 85 and 86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A, while the presumption is under BSA Section 118, corresponding to Evidence Act Section 113B.
accepted.tq: Match the new BNS provision with its former IPC counterpart.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: For the purpose of the offence of dowry death, death occurring within what period from the date of marriage is specifically relevant?
accepted.x: BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs within seven years of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory time-limit as the decisive numerical clue.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s:
The amendments of 1984 and 1986 to the dowry-related legal framework are significant because the 1986 changes brought in:
1. The offence of dowry death under Section 304B of the IPC.
2. The presumption relating to dowry death under Section 113B of the Evidence Act.
3. The exclusion of mahr from the definition of dowry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 1986 changes introduced dowry death under IPC Section 304B and the presumption under Evidence Act Section 113B. The exclusion of mahr forms part of the statutory definition and was not the stated significance of the 1986 changes.
accepted.tq: Separate the amendment-specific developments from an independent definitional provision.
accepted.sec: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

accepted.s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, the maternity benefit for the third child onwards is:
accepted.x: The 2017 position provides 12 weeks of maternity benefit for the third child onwards. The longer period applies to the first two children.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the benefit applicable to later children from the first-two-children provision.
accepted.sec: Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 - leave, adoptive/commissioning mothers, creche, work from home

accepted.s: A woman adopting a child below three months of age is entitled under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 to maternity benefit for:
o: Six weeks from the date of adoption
Twelve weeks from the date the child is handed over to her
Twenty-six weeks from the date of adoption in every case
Eight weeks before the adoption and four weeks after it
accepted.x: An adopting mother of a child below three months is entitled to 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to her. The same 12-week period applies to a commissioning mother.
accepted.tq: Focus on both the eligibility condition and the statutory starting point.
accepted.sec: Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 - leave, adoptive/commissioning mothers, creche, work from home

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the maternity benefit for a commissioning mother under the 2017 amendment?
o: Six weeks from the date of commissioning, with no post-handover entitlement
Twelve weeks from the date the child is handed over to her
Twelve weeks beginning three months before delivery
Twenty-six weeks irrespective of the number of children
accepted.x: A commissioning mother is entitled to 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to her. The provision is not framed as a pre-delivery benefit or as an unconditional 26-week benefit.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between biological-mother leave and the adoptive or commissioning-mother rule.
accepted.sec: Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 - leave, adoptive/commissioning mothers, creche, work from home

accepted.s: A crèche facility is mandatory under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 in an establishment having:
o: 20 or more employees, with two visits a day
100 or more employees, with one visit a day
30 or more employees, with three visits a day
50 or more employees, with four visits a day
accepted.x: The amendment requires a crèche in establishments having 50 or more employees. The woman is to be allowed four visits a day to the crèche.
accepted.tq: Combine the threshold number with the associated statutory frequency.
accepted.sec: Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 - leave, adoptive/commissioning mothers, creche, work from home

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding work from home under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017:
1. It may be allowed after the period of maternity leave.
2. It is available where the nature of work permits it.
3. It requires mutual agreement between the woman and the employer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Work from home may be permitted after maternity leave where the nature of work allows it and where there is mutual agreement between the woman and the employer. Thus all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the cumulative conditions rather than treating work from home as an automatic right.
accepted.sec: Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 - leave, adoptive/commissioning mothers, creche, work from home

accepted.s:
Which of the following chronological orders of enactment is correct?
A. Dowry Prohibition Act
B. Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act
C. Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act
D. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act
accepted.x: The years are 1961 for the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1986 for the Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1987 for the Commission of Sati Act and 2006 for the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.
accepted.tq: Arrange the enactments by their years, checking the close 1986–1987 sequence.

accepted.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was originally known as SITA and was amended in:
accepted.x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1956 after being known as SITA and was amended in 1986. The year 1986 should not be mistaken for its original enactment year.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original enactment year from the amendment year.
accepted.sec: Other women-specific laws → year

accepted.s: The PCPNDT Act is associated with which of the following pairs of years?
o: 1994; the PNDT law was renamed in 2003
accepted.x: The law was enacted in 1994 as the PNDT Act and was renamed the PCPNDT Act in 2003.
accepted.tq: Test the enactment year separately from the later renaming year.
accepted.sec: Other women-specific laws → year

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act — 2006
Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act — 1987; came into force in 1988
accepted.x: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1987 and came into force in 1988. The Indecent Representation Act dates to 1986, the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act to 2006 and the Muslim Women Act concerning triple talaq to 2019.
accepted.tq: Use neighbouring enactment years to expose swapped law-year pairs.
accepted.sec: Other women-specific laws → year

accepted.s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, dealing with the practice of triple talaq, was passed on:
accepted.x: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was passed on 30 July 2019.
accepted.tq: Test the precise date rather than merely the year of enactment.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act bans denigrating depiction of women in advertisements and publications.
2. Monitoring under the law has been extended to digital and AI-generated content.
3. The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification of sati.
4. A District Magistrate may seize property used for glorification of sati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Indecent Representation law covers denigrating depiction and, as of 2025, monitoring extends to digital and AI-generated content. The Sati Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification, and permits the District Magistrate to seize property used for glorification.
accepted.tq: Combine provisions from two related women-protection laws while checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: Other women-specific laws → year
